title: Flat local finite type becomes local finite presentation from a dense open
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], and let $X,Y$ be algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space] in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Morphism properties use [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties]; locally finite type is the chart test with [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Fibre products are sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Let $f:X\to Y$ be flat and locally of finite type, and let $j:V\hookrightarrow Y$ be an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion]. Assume $j$ is quasi-compact, meaning every affine etale scheme chart of $Y$ has quasi-compact inverse image of $V$, and schematically dense, meaning $\mathcal O_Y\to j_*\mathcal O_V$ is injective on the small etale site. Suppose $X\times_YV\to V$ is locally of finite presentation. Then $f$ is locally of finite presentation. No separatedness or quasi-compactness hypothesis on $f$ is imposed.

proof.text: Test the conclusion on an arbitrary compatible pair of etale scheme charts $a:U\to X$, $b:T\to Y$ and $h:U\to T$ with $fa=bh$. By the chart definitions, $h$ is flat and locally of finite type. Put $W=T\times_YV$, an open subscheme of $T$. Every affine open $T_0\subset T$ is again an etale chart of $Y$, so $W\cap T_0$ is quasi-compact by the hypothesis on $j$. Thus $W$ is retrocompact: cover any quasi-compact open of $T$ by finitely many affine opens and take their intersections with $W$. Schematic density is also inherited directly: evaluating the assumed monomorphism $\mathcal O_Y\to j_*\mathcal O_V$ on any etale scheme over $T$ gives the injective restriction to its intersection with $W$. In particular this holds on all Zariski opens of $T$. Finally $h^{-1}W\to W$ is locally of finite presentation: its source and target maps to $X_V$ and $V$ are restrictions of the given charts, so this is precisely a chart test for the hypothesis on $f_V$. It suffices to prove local finite presentation of this arbitrary $h$.

source.place: Tag 0877, proof via Tag 0876: etale chart reduction; schematic density evaluated on the small etale site.

proof.text: Work over an affine open $T_0=\operatorname{Spec}A$ of $T$. By the definition of locally finite type, $h^{-1}T_0$ has an affine open cover by $Z=\operatorname{Spec}B$ with $B$ a finite-type $A$-algebra. Fix one such $Z$ and a surjection $q:P=A[t_1,\ldots,t_n]\twoheadrightarrow B$. Put $H=\operatorname{Spec}P$, $p:H\to T_0$ and $F=\widetilde B$ as an $\mathcal O_H$-module. The morphism $p$ is locally of finite presentation, since the displayed polynomial algebra has a presentation with $n$ generators and no relations. The sheaf $F$ is quasi-coherent, and is of finite type: $B$ is generated by $1$ as a $P$-module, so the affine finite-type criterion applies. The associated-sheaf sections formula (with the inverted element $1$) identifies $\Gamma(H,F)=B$. Write $W_0=W\cap T_0$; the preceding step gives precisely the retrocompactness and schematic density of $W_0\subset T_0$.

source.place: Tag 081P, affine reduction and closed embedding in affine n-space; Tag 081N hypotheses for the associated cyclic polynomial module.

proof.text: Flatness of $h$ gives that $B$ is flat over $A$, by the affine criterion for flat morphisms on $Z\subset U$ and $T_0\subset T$. Apply the affine-chart relative-flatness criterion to $p:H\to T_0$, the quasi-coherent sheaf $F$, and the affine open $H$ itself: its section module is the $A$-flat module $B$, so every stalk $F_z$ is flat over $\mathcal O_{T_0,p(z)}$. This is exactly relative flatness of $F$ over $T_0$. This argument applies also at points of $H$ outside the closed support of $F$, where the stalk is zero; it assumes no finite presentation for $B$ over $A$.

source.place: Tag 081P, omitted verification that i_* O_Z is base-flat; Morphisms Tag 01U4 (lemma-flat-module-characterize).

proof.text: For every principal open $D(a)\subset W_0$ in $\operatorname{Spec}A$, the morphism $\operatorname{Spec}B_a\to\operatorname{Spec}A_a$ is a restriction of $h^{-1}W\to W$. The affine-opens finite-presentation theorem therefore says that $B_a$ is a finitely presented $A_a$-algebra. The localized surjection $P_a=A_a[t_1,\ldots,t_n]\twoheadrightarrow B_a$ has finitely generated kernel by the independence-of-presentation theorem. If $r_1,\ldots,r_m$ generate that kernel, the sequence $P_a^m\to P_a\to B_a\to0$, whose first map sends $(c_i)$ to $\sum_i c_i r_i$, is an explicit finite presentation of the $P_a$-module $B_a$. The associated-sections localization formula identifies this module with the sections of $F$ on $p^{-1}D(a)=\operatorname{Spec}P_a$. By the affine sheaf criterion $F$ is finitely presented there. Principal opens $D(a)\subset W_0$ cover $W_0$, so these presentations give finite presentation of $F|_{p^{-1}W_0}$.

source.place: Tag 081P, omitted verification over the open; Algebra Tag 00R2 (lemma-finite-presentation-independent); Properties Tag 01PC (lemma-finite-presentation-module).

proof.text: Apply the existing module extension theorem to $p:H\to T_0$, $F$ and $W_0$. Its hypotheses have all been verified: $p$ is locally of finite presentation, $F$ is finite type and flat over $T_0$, $W_0$ is retrocompact and schematically dense, and $F$ is finitely presented over $W_0$. It follows that $F$ is of finite presentation on all of $H$. The affine finite-presentation criterion then gives that $B=\Gamma(H,F)$ is a finitely presented $P$-module.

source.place: Tag 081P, apply Tag 081N to i_* O_Z; Properties Tag 01PC for global sections.

proof.text: Apply the surjective-module kernel theorem to the $P$-linear surjection $P\twoheadrightarrow B$: its source is generated by $1$ and its target is finitely presented by the preceding step. Consequently $I=\ker q$ is finitely generated as a $P$-submodule, equivalently as an ideal. Choosing ideal generators $g_1,\ldots,g_r$ gives $B\cong A[t_1,\ldots,t_n]/(g_1,\ldots,g_r)$ as $A$-algebras. Thus $Z\to T_0$ is locally of finite presentation by its definition. These $Z$ cover $h^{-1}T_0$, and the $T_0$ cover $T$, so every point has the required affine presentation: $h$ is locally of finite presentation. Since the initial compatible charts were arbitrary, the chart definition gives local finite presentation of $f$. Only affine open pieces of charts were used; neither separatedness nor quasi-compactness of $f$ was required.

tool_uses.why: Tag 081N for a relatively flat finite-type module on polynomial affine space is the precise engine of the Tag 081P proof; it is a generic module finiteness theorem, not the trace-formula unit argument.
The generic affine section/stalk equivalence verifies base-flatness of the cyclic polynomial module; it replaces no step of the present unit.
The generic associated-sheaf localization formula identifies sections of the cyclic polynomial module before and after principal base restriction.
The generic affine criterion converts the chart morphism flatness hypothesis to A-flatness of its coordinate algebra.
The general affine module/sheaf finite-type and finite-presentation equivalences translate the polynomial-module argument.
Independence of a finite algebra presentation is needed over each principal open for the fixed polynomial surjection.
The generic composition/open-immersion statements verify that restrictions of scheme charts remain charts.
The existing general fibre-product statement forms restrictions of the given etale charts over the open subspace.
